close_reason: Recommendation ratified after no human pushback in ~46 hours; direction is option (i) (migrate inline unit tests + delete MockBackend). Implementation scope (40 tests + 350-line module deletion across 3+ files) exceeds the '>3 files = file an epic, get approval' workspace rule, so the actual migration is now tracked on JMAP-826m.55 with its own human-label authorization.
description:
Scenario: Maintenance pattern for unit-test infrastructure varies across the workspace. mail-server (canonical) has NO inline #[cfg(test)] unit tests in src/*.rs — only integration tests in tests/. metadata-server has both: inline #[cfg(test)] in src/metadata.rs (lines 645+) backed by a 350-line MockBackend in src/lib.rs (lines 122-477), AND integration tests in tests/ backed by the public MemoryBackend.

Maintenance burden:
(a) Two backends, two trait impls, two test surfaces. When the MetadataBackend or JmapBackend trait grows a method (e.g. principal_id was added to JmapBackend at JMAP-ga0q.1), BOTH MockBackend and MemoryBackend need updates.

(b) MockBackend's get_objects (lib.rs:282-287) does a serde_json::to_value(&m) + from_value(v) round-trip to convert Metadata to a generic O. This 'serde-round-trip downcast' is genuinely subtle and the inline tests rely on it. A contributor adding a non-trivial JmapObject impl that doesn't survive the round-trip will hit a confusing error.

(c) MockBackend's get_changes (lib.rs:301-337) implements a simplified 'all-or-nothing' returning all recorded changes if since_state != current. This does not exercise the real cursor semantics, so the inline tests that pre-populate the change log are essentially 'fake' — they bypass the dedup algorithm and just trust whatever's in the change log vectors.

(d) The 'identical to sharing-server's mock pattern' comment (lib.rs:281) reinforces the wrong canonical (see finding JMAP-826m.11).

Resolution options:
(i) Drop the inline unit tests and inline test_support module. Move all tests to tests/ using MemoryBackend. Pros: single test surface, fewer trait impls to keep in sync. Cons: loses fine-grained unit testing for the cross-field filter validator and the destroy validate-and-collect.
(ii) Move test_support out of src/lib.rs into tests/common/mod.rs (alongside the existing common module). Pros: stops cluttering library compilation, keeps unit-test capability. Cons: integration tests cannot easily test crate-private items.
(iii) Accept the duplication and document the canonical workspace pattern (this is what option (a) effectively is now).
title: test_support::MockBackend is pub(crate) in src/lib.rs, gated #[cfg(test)] but lives in the main crate compilation — adds 350+ lines, two extra trait impls, a serde_json round-trip downcast, and an explicit per-method comment claiming 'identical to sharing-server'
